q: Takens' theorem (1981) on delay embeddings: for a smooth dynamical system on a compact manifold M of dimension d, the delay-coordinate map using 2d+1 time delays is generically an embedding. The proof uses Sard's theorem to show that:
opts: The map is always a diffeomorphism
The set of 'bad' observation functions (those for which the delay map is not an embedding) has measure zero in the space of smooth functions
The manifold M must be a sphere
exp: Takens' proof: the 'bad' set of functions h: M → ℝ for which (h(x), h(Tx),..., h(T^{2d}x)) fails to be an embedding has measure zero by Sard's theorem and Whitney's embedding theorem. So generically 2d+1 delays suffice. Extensions (Sauer-Yorke-Casdagli) handle fractal attractors: 2·dim_H(A)+1 delays suffice.
